clinician.trajectory_summary: A 17-year-old male presented with a one-month history of polyurea, polydipsia, general weakness, and pallor, on a background of bilateral progressive sensorineural hearing loss since childhood, short stature, and no weight gain for three years. Physical examination on admission revealed the characteristic constellation of H syndrome features: short stature, hallux valgus, hyperpigmented plaques with clear borders (painful on palpation), dilated lateral scleral vessels, splenomegaly, Boutonniere deformity of hands and toes, scrotal mass, underdeveloped small penis with testicular volume 3 cm bilaterally, and absent pubic/axillary hair. Audiological examination confirmed profound bilateral sensorineural hearing loss.
